requirements.requirement: Join node1, node2, and node3 into a single RabbitMQ cluster
requirements.summary: Erlang 27.3.4.16 and RabbitMQ 4.3.5 installed on all three nodes; node2 and node3 successfully joined node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster after resolving firewall connectivity issues, and rabbitmqctl cluster_status on node1 shows all three nodes as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with matching RabbitMQ/Erlang versions.
rabbitmqctl add_vhost payments succeeded and list_vhosts confirms payments exists alongside the default vhost.

requirements.requirement: Application account able to publish and consume in the payments vhost
requirements.summary: app_payments user created with configure/write/read '.*' permissions scoped to payments (no admin tags); a pika AMQP client using app_payments credentials successfully published and then consumed (basic_get+ack) a message on the orders queue.

requirements.requirement: Messages published to a durable queue survive the loss of any one node and stay consumable from the remaining nodes
requirements.summary: A durable quorum queue 'orders' (replicated across all 3 nodes) received 3 durable messages; node3 (a non-leader replica) was stopped via systemctl stop while node1/node2 continued running (quorum preserved, confirmed via cluster_status on node2 showing only node1/node2 as Running Nodes); all 3 messages were successfully basic_get+ack'd from node2 while node3 was down, directly demonstrating survival of node loss and continued consumability. Node3 was then restarted and rejoined cleanly.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node (independent check)
requirements.summary: For each of node1, node2, node3: pre-restart boot_id and active rabbitmq-server were captured, systemctl reboot was acknowledged, the node became unreachable and then returned with a different boot_id (cross-checked against the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot for all three nodes), rabbitmq-server was confirmed active, and cluster/queue state (HTTP API showing orders queue 'running' with all 3 members online) was verified recovered. Node1 and node3 additionally had explicit post-restart publish/consume tests via the app account; node2's recovery was confirmed via HTTP API queue and node status only, without a dedicated fresh pub/sub round-trip immediately after its own restart (a subsequent node3 test came after all three restarts and covered the account/queue end-to-end).

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster was formed, the payments vhost and app_payments account were created with correct scoped permissions, and a durable quorum queue was directly shown to survive the stop of one node (2/3 quorum preserved) with all messages remaining consumable from the surviving nodes. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with matching pre/post boot identities, service recovery, and cluster/queue health confirmation, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Minor hygiene issues (an unused epel-release install and a broken rabbitmqadmin binary left in /usr/local/bin) were not cleaned up but pose low risk.
limitations: Node2's post-restart recovery evidence relies on cluster/queue HTTP API state rather than an immediate dedicated publish/consume round-trip specific to that node, though overall functional recovery was later reconfirmed via node3.

The first node3 post-restart publish/consume attempt (cmd-056915ec768e4384) returned no message, likely due to a timing race after copying the password file; this was resolved on retry (cmd-f5d886a2c3b94c22), but the transient failure is noted for completeness.
Full package-manager consistency output and complete journalctl history are truncated in some captured evidence, limiting deep verification of underlying system health beyond what was reported.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were clearly tied to the task (package installs, firewall port openings for clustering, cookie distribution, cluster join, vhost/user/queue creation, resilience test with stop/start of node3, sequential reboots). Two minor unnecessary residues were left behind and not cleaned up: (1) on node1, epel-release was installed (cmd-3a8d342450f34beb) as part of an abandoned installation approach that was never used for the final RabbitMQ/Erlang install path, and remained installed; (2) on node1, a failed rabbitmqadmin download (cmd-f487f63d24004de5) left a bogus non-executable-content file at /usr/local/bin/rabbitmqadmin marked executable, which was never removed or corrected. Both are low-risk, bounded residue rather than destructive or security-weakening changes. Temporary password files were consistently shredded after use (cmd-1a95fd43a2f24cbc, cmd-d327d7ebbaf24d47, cmd-f5d886a2c3b94c22, cmd-77972ab894404ae0), and the node3 stop/start during the resilience test was a bounded, intentional, and fully restored action.
